text: Three hours, then two. A day is as long as a movie.
At a three hour day the Sun crosses the sky in ninety minutes, sliding its own width every sixteen seconds.
The ground moves at about eighty-three hundred miles an hour.
You weigh twenty-two percent less: a hundred and fifty pounds feels like a hundred and seventeen.
At two hours, you weigh half.
The jump that lifts you a foot and a half now lifts you about three feet.
The Sun crosses the whole sky in an hour.
Every object near the equator is half as heavy as it should be, and buildings, bridges and oceans must hold on with half the force.
If you're enjoying this, tap like and follow.

text: At an hour and a half, you're almost weightless.
